sources.note: Nothing. Covers consonants, vowels, rhymes, tones (Wucun dialect: 3 level, 2 falling, 1 rising toneme; Shangyao dialect per de Sousa 2011: 4 level, 1 falling, 2 rising), tone sandhi (24 -> 33 before another tone in disyllables), syllable structure. The only 'accent' hits are 'dialects as accents of one another'. No word stress / prominence / neutral tone statement.

en: Nanning Pinghua tone chart (six tones in open syllables, four in checked), lateral fricative; nothing on stress or neutral tone. zh: 桂南平话 nine tones 52/44/55/21/24/22/4/24/2 'same system as Guangzhou'; nothing on stress.

sources.note: 84-page areal-typological sketch whose Nanning (Shangyao) Pinghua phonology is the standard English-language source (Cao 2018 takes its Shangyao consonant, vowel, rhyme and tone data from de Sousa); as an MSEA-areal treatment it is the most likely place for an explicit remark on stress/prominence or its absence in a tonal Sinitic language.

sources.note: The only full-length modern phonology of a Southern Pinghua dialect (Wucun, Nanning) in English; a thesis-length phonology normally has a suprasegmentals section that would state whether word stress exists. Not in UNE's RUNE repository at run time; may be obtainable from the author (RMIT) or UNE library.
